kjv: the man spake unto Ithiel, even unto Ithiel and Ucal
mine: The man declares: I am weary, O God; I am weary, O God, and worn out
note: The consonants l'yty'l l'yty'l w'kl can be read as names (MT vocalisation) or as la'iti 'el ... wa'ekel "I am weary, O God ... and worn out", which fits the confession of ignorance in vv. 2–3. Context: I am weary, O God (medium confidence). 30:2-3 'I am more brutish than any man ... I have not learned wisdom' continues a confession of exhaustion.
Hebrew shephannim are rock hyraxes, native to Palestine; "coney" meant a rabbit, which does not live in cliffs.

kjv: The spider taketh hold with her hands
mine: the lizard you can take in your hands
note: Hebrew semamit is a gecko or lizard; the verb can mean "you can catch it in your hands".

kjv: A greyhound ... a king, against whom [there is] no rising up
mine: the strutting rooster ... a king with his army around him
note: Hebrew zarzir motnayim ("girded of loins") is uncertain, often a rooster; 'alqum is obscure, often taken as "army, troop" (Arabic al-qawm).
